sentences.text: Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Learned counsel for the appellant does not wish to press I.A.No.13897 of 2024, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

Accordingly,
I.A.No.13897/2024, is dismissed as not pressed.
2. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, this appeal is heard finally.

3. According to Section 42 of Act, the 4 of accused is not being given additional POCSO ---- ---- punishment because he has been Act, 2012 sentenced u/s 6 of POCSO Act.
6 of Additional POCSO RI for 20 years Rs.20,000/- RI for 1 Act, 2012 year 3
. It is submitted that appellant is innocent.
Victim is a consenting adult as can be seen from the evidence of her father (PW-3), who has admitted that he got her daughter admitted in the school at the age of 09- 10 years.

It is, thus, submitted that date of birth mentioned in Dakhila Kharij Register (Ex.P/39) as 10/09/2007 showing her admission in Class-I is inappropriate inasmuch as in the light of the statement of PW- 3, her date of birth will be somewhere in 2002-03 and, therefore, victim NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55240 3 CRA-6807-2024 was a consenting adult on the date of incident i.e. 18/07/2021.
4.
It is submitted that lady doctor (PW-8) has also not supported the case of the prosecution and has not given any definite opinion in regard to violation of privacy.

It is further pointed out that Dr.
Shashikala Marko (PW-8) had advised X-ray for age determination of the victim, but no X-ray report has been brought on record by the prosecution and, therefore, in the light of the judgment of the Supreme Court in Sunil vs. State of Haryana, (2010) 1 SCC 742, in absence of X-ray examination which determine the age, conviction of the appellant cannot be maintained.

sentences.text: Shri Nitin Gupta, learned Public Prosecutor for the State, in his turn, submits that DNA report (Ex.P/45) is positive and, therefore, no indulgence is called for.
6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident that the victim (PW-1) has stated that all the accused persons are known to her.
Accused Sahu Baiga had violated her privacy.
He had kept her for three days.
Amarkantak Police had come and taken her.
In cross-examination, she admits that accused Dasri Bai and Ayatu are sister and brother in-law of accused Sahu Baiga.
She further admits that accused Sahu Baiga had taken her on foot.
When he had brought her to the house of his sister Dasri Bai then she had met two persons Dasri Bai and Ayatu Baiga.
She admits that Ayatu is brother of her father in relationship.
She further admits that Dasri Bai and Ayatu had not put any prohibition on her movement and she was free to work without asking NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55240 4 CRA-6807-2024 them.
She further admits that when she had stayed along with Sahu Baiga in the house of Phoolmat Bai then her father was having intimation of such stay and he had not come to take her.
7. Father of the victim (PW-3) in Para-3 of his statement admits that at the time of admission in the school, the age of victim was 09-10 years.
Dakhila Kharij Register (Ex.P/39) reveals that victim was admitted in school on 20/06/2013 and there is overwriting in the date of birth of the victim.
8 . School Teacher (PW-17) has admitted that victim was admitted on 20/06/2013 in Class-I.
He has admitted that there is correction in the date of birth.
9. Dr. Shashikala Marko (PW-8) has stated that hymen of the victim was old torn.
She had advised X-ray of right elbow, right knee and right iliac crest test for age determination.
She refused to give any definite opinion in regard to violation of privacy, however Ex.P/45 is the DNA report which is positive.
10. Thus, what is to be examine is whether at the time of the incident victim was a minor or not.
11. When tested then in the light of evidence of victim's father (PW- 3), he got her daughter admitted in Class-I in 2013 when her age was 09-10 years.
Thus, date of birth of the victim will be between 2003-04.
12. Dr. Shashikala Marko (PW-8) had advised X-ray examination for determination of age of the victim.
School Teacher (PW-17) has admitted overwriting in the date of birth of the victim.

Thus,
when these NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55240 5 CRA-6807-2024 facts are taken into consideration then in the light of judgment of Supreme Court in Sunil (supra), where it is held that "the failure of getting the prosecutrix examined from the dental surgeon or the radiologist despite the fact that she was referred to them by doctor is a serious flaw in the prosecution version.
It is further held that we are not laid down as a rule that all these test must be performed in all cases,
but in the instant case, in the absence of primary evidence, reports of the dental surgeon and the radiologist would have helped in arriving at the conclusion regarding the age of the prosecutrix."

sentences.text:
Thus, it is evident that despite proper advised by the lady doctor PW-8, not carrying out radiological examination to determine the age, especially in the backdrop of doubtful circumstances,
where father of the victim (PW-3) admits that at the time of admission age of the victim was 09-10 years, and School Teacher (PW-17) admits interpolation in the year of birth then in the light of the judgment of Supreme Court in Sunil (supra), we are of the opinion that prosecution having failed to prove that victim was a minor, benefit of doubt will be accrued in favour of the appellant and,
therefore, impugned judgment of conviction cannot be sustained despite the fact that DNA report is positive because a consensual relationship between two adults resulting in a positive DNA, cannot be a sufficient ground to upheld conviction under sections 363, 366-A, 376(2)(J), 376(2)(n), 376 of IPC and Section 4 & 6 of POCSO Act.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:55240 6 CRA-6807-2024 14.
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment dated 25/04/2024 passed by learned trial Court is set aside.
Appellant be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
15. Case property be disposed off in terms of the orders of the learned trial Court.
